{"additions":2018,"author":{"id":"U_kgDODaWbcA","is_bot":false,"login":"njpiombino","name":"Nicholas Piombino"},"baseRefName":"develop","body":"## Summary\n\n**What**\n\nStore managers can now list only low-stock or out-of-stock inventory items from the existing admin inventory list. Results are sorted by lowest available quantity first.\n\n- `GET /admin/inventory-items` accepts `stock_status` (`low_stock`, `out_of_stock`, or both). Filtering, sorting, paging and counts happen in the database query.\n- The admin inventory list has a \"Stock status\" filter and new **Available** and **Low stock threshold** columns.\n- Mutation testing (D6) setup and reports for this issue are included.\n\n**Why**\n\nCloses #62. Managers had to scan every item to find what needs restocking. This uses the per-item threshold from #61 to show only items that are low or out of stock.\n\n**How**\n\n- **Inventory module:** `listInventoryItems` / `listAndCountInventoryItems` handle a `stock_status` filter. A `GROUP BY` / `HAVING` query finds matching item ids, sorted by available quantity (stocked minus reserved, summed over locations, lowest first). The ids are intersected with the other filters, the requested page is taken, and the page is loaded with the caller's fields and relations. Without `stock_status`, the methods behave exactly as before.\n- **API:** `stock_status` added to the list validator (outside `$and` / `$or`) and to `AdminInventoryItemsParams` / `FilterableInventoryItemProps`.\n- **Dashboard:** status filter, query param, Available and threshold columns, and a \"Stock status\" translation key. The empty filtered list uses the table's existing \"No results\" state.\n- **Dev tooling:** StrykerJS 10.1.1 and its Jest runner added as root dev dependencies; Stryker output added to `.gitignore`.\n\nA changeset is included (patch).\n\n**Testing**\n\nSee **Test Evidence** below. To reproduce (Postgres running):\n\n```bash\nyarn workspace @medusajs/types build && yarn workspace @medusajs/inventory build && yarn workspace @medusajs/medusa build\ncd packages/modules/inventory && npx jest integration-tests\ncd integration-tests/http && npx jest __tests__/inventory/admin/inventory.spec.ts __tests__/reservations\ncd packages/admin/dashboard && npx vitest run src/routes/inventory\ncd packages/modules/inventory && npx stryker run   # mutation testing\n```\n\nManual (`my-store`, after rebuilding `@medusajs/dashboard`): open Inventory in the admin, add the \"Stock status\" filter, choose \"Out of stock\", then open an item. Lower an item's stock to see it move into the filtered list.\n\n---\n\n## Examples\n\n```ts\n// Out-of-stock items first, then low stock, each group lowest available first\nconst { inventory_items, count } = await sdk.admin.inventoryItem.list({\n  stock_status: [\"low_stock\", \"out_of_stock\"],\n  limit: 20,\n})\n```\n\n`GET /admin/inventory-items?stock_status[]=low_stock&stock_status[]=out_of_stock`\n\n---\n\n## Design\n\n**Decision:** Filter by stock status on the server through the existing inventory list endpoint, and expose it as a filter on the existing admin inventory list.\n\n**Alternatives considered:**\n- Filter in the dashboard only. Rejected: `stocked_quantity` / `reserved_quantity` are computed SUM fields, so filtering one page of 20 in the browser gives part-empty pages and wrong counts.\n- A separate `/inventory/low-stock` page or a tab. Rejected: it needs a new route and table but does nothing the filtered list doesn't. Open question 1, agreed in the issue discussion.\n- One row per item and location. Rejected by the team to keep scope; the threshold is per item (#61). Possible follow-up.\n\n**Rationale:** One query parameter on an existing endpoint gives correct paging and counts with no new route. The dashboard change is a filter and two columns on a table managers already use.\n\n**Consequences:**\n- While `stock_status` is set, results are always sorted by available quantity, and any `order` in the request is ignored.\n- Each filtered request loads the id of every item with the status (see Tech Debt).\n\n**Other decisions:**\n- **Status is per item:** available quantity = stocked minus reserved, summed over all locations, compared with the item's `low_stock_threshold`. This is the same rule as `getStockStatus` from #61. Items with no location levels are out of stock. A threshold of 0 never shows low stock.\n- **Sort by lowest available quantity** (open question 2). The alternative, distance below threshold, ranks items oddly when the threshold is 0. Ties are broken by id.\n- **Available column added:** acceptance criterion 3 requires the available quantity, and the list only showed reserved and in-stock counts. The alternative was relying on the existing columns and expecting managers to subtract.\n- **`stock_status` not allowed inside `$and` / `$or`:** the service handles it only at the top level. The alternative was supporting nested status filters, which nobody needs.\n- **Location filter:** the existing location filter still works alongside `stock_status`, but status is always computed over all locations.\n\n---\n\n## Tech Debt\n\n**Introduced:**\n- The filter loads every matching item id per request to keep the quantity order across pages. This is fine for normal catalogs; it is marked with a `shortcut:` comment in `inventory-module.ts` with when to move the sort fully into SQL.\n- `packages/modules/inventory/stryker-build.cjs` works around a Babel bug in the mutation testing setup: Stryker's instrumenter drops `@MedusaContext()` parameter decorators. The workaround is only used by `stryker run`.\n\n**Encountered:**\n- `moduleIntegrationTestRunner` wraps suites in `describe(\"\")`, which breaks Stryker's per-test coverage, so the config uses `coverageAnalysis: \"all\"`.\n- Module and HTTP tests run against `dist/`, so packages must be rebuilt before testing source changes.\n- The dashboard typecheck has 6 errors in `packages/core/types` with or without this PR; left as

+  @InjectManager()
+  // @ts-expect-error
+  async listInventoryItems(
+    filters: InventoryTypes.FilterableInventoryItemProps = {},
+    config: FindConfig<InventoryTypes.InventoryItemDTO> = {},
+    @MedusaContext() context: Context = {}
+  ): Promise<InventoryTypes.InventoryItemDTO[]> {
+    if (!filters.stock_status) {
+      return await super.listInventoryItems(filters, config, context)
+    }
+
+    const [items] = await this.listAndCountInventoryItems(

+      config,

+
+  @InjectManager()
+  // @ts-expect-error
+  async listAndCountInventoryItems(
+    filters: InventoryTypes.FilterableInventoryItemProps = {},
+    config: FindConfig<InventoryTypes.InventoryItemDTO> = {},
+    @MedusaContext() context: Context = {}
+  ): Promise<[InventoryTypes.InventoryItemDTO[], number]> {
+    const { stock_status, ...otherFilters } = filters
+
+    if (!stock_status) {
+      return await super.listAndCountInventoryItems(filters, config, context)
+    }
+
+    const sortedIds = await this.listIdsByStockStatus_(stock_status, context)
+    if (!sortedIds.length) {
+      return [[], 0]
+    }
+
+    // shortcut: loads every matching id to keep the quantity order across pages, move the sort into SQL if catalogs reach tens of thousands of low-stock items
+    const matching = await this.inventoryItemService_.list(
+      { $and: [otherFilters, { id: sortedIds }] },
+      { select: ["id"] },
+      context
+    )
+    const matchingIds = new Set(matching.map((item) => item.id))
+    const ids = sortedIds.filter((id) => matchingIds.has(id))
+
+    const skip = config.skip ?? 0
+    const pageIds = ids.slice(
+      skip,
+      config.take == null ? undefined : skip + config.take
+    )
+    if (!pageIds.length) {
+      return [[], ids.length]
+    }
+
+    const items = await super.listInventoryItems(
+      { id: pageIds },
+      { ...config, skip: undefined, take: undefined, order: undefined },
+      context
+    )
+    const itemsById = new Map(items.map((item) => [item.id, item]))
+
+    return [pageIds.map((id) => itemsById.get(id)!), ids.length]
+  }
+
+  /**
+   * Returns the ids of inventory items with the given stock statuses, sorted by
+   * total available quantity (stocked - reserved), lowest first. Mirrors the
+   * dashboard's `getStockStatus`.
+   */
+  protected async listIdsByStockStatus_(
+    stockStatus:
+      | InventoryTypes.InventoryStockStatus
+      | InventoryTypes.InventoryStockStatus[],
+    context: Context
+  ): Promise<string[]> {
+    const available =
+      "COALESCE(SUM(il.stocked_quantity), 0) - COALESCE(SUM(il.reserved_quantity), 0)"
+    const conditions: Record<InventoryTypes.InventoryStockStatus, string> = {
+      out_of_stock: `${available} <= 0`,
+      low_stock: `${available} > 0 AND ${available} <= ii.low_stock_threshold`,
+    }
+
+    const statuses = Array.isArray(stockStatus) ? stockStatus : [stockStatus]
+    const invalid = statuses.filter((status) => !(status in conditions))
+    if (invalid.length) {
+      throw new MedusaError(
+        MedusaError.Types.INVALID_DATA,
+        `Invalid stock status: ${invalid.join(", ")}`
+      )
+    }
+
+    const manager = (context.transactionManager ??
+      context.manager) as SqlEntityManager
+    const knex = manager.getTransactionContext() ?? manager.getKnex()
+
+    const rows: { id: string }[] = await knex("inventory_item as ii")
+      .leftJoin("inventory_level as il", (join) =>
+        join.on("il.inventory_item_id", "ii.id").andOnNull("il.deleted_at")
+      )
+      .whereNull("ii.deleted_at")
+      .groupBy("ii.id")
+      .havingRaw(
+        statuses.map((status) => `(${conditions[status]})`).join(" OR ")
+      )
+      .orderByRaw(`${available} ASC, ii.id ASC`)
+      .select("ii.id")
+
+    return rows.map((row) => row.id)
+  }

diff --git a/packages/modules/inventory/stryker-build.cjs b/packages/modules/inventory/stryker-build.cjs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..2e5de7b39f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/packages/modules/inventory/stryker-build.cjs
@@ -0,0 +1,20 @@
+// Stryker buildCommand for issue #62 mutation testing.
+// Babel, which Stryker uses to instrument the file, drops parameter decorators
+// on parameters that have a default value, so every `@MedusaContext() context:
+// Context = {}` loses its decorator and @EmitEvents fails at runtime. This puts
+// them back before building dist/, which the module tests load.
+const fs = require("fs")
+const { execSync } = require("child_process")
+
+const file = "src/services/inventory-module.ts"
+const pattern = /(?<!@MedusaContext\(\) )\bcontext: Context = \{\}/g
+
+const source = fs.readFileSync(file, "utf8")
+const restored = (source.match(pattern) ?? []).length
+fs.writeFileSync(
+  file,
+  source.replace(pattern, "@MedusaContext() context: Context = {}")
+)
+console.log(`stryker-build: restored ${restored} @MedusaContext() decorators`)
+
+execSync("yarn build", { stdio: "inherit" })

+{
+  "$schema": "../../../node_modules/@stryker-mutator/core/schema/stryker-schema.json",
+  "_comment": "Issue #62 mutation testing (D6). Run from this directory with Postgres up: npx stryker run. Mutates only the lines added for #62. The module tests load dist/, so the instrumented source is rebuilt before testing; inPlace because the sandbox copy breaks tsconfig's relative extends. Concurrency 1 because every test run uses the same test database name. coverageAnalysis is 'all' because moduleIntegrationTestRunner wraps suites in describe(\"\"), so perTest coverage ids never match Jest's test names and every mutant shows as uncovered.",
+  "packageManager": "yarn",
+  "testRunner": "jest",
+  "jest": {
+    "projectType": "custom",

+      ]

+  },

## What the PR does
It adds a `stock_status` filter (`low_stock` / `out_of_stock`) to `GET /admin/inventory-items`. Results are sorted by available quantity, lowest first.
- A `GROUP BY` / `HAVING` query in the inventory module finds the matching item ids.
- The ids are intersected with the other filters, paged in memory, and loaded with the caller's fields.
- Requests without `stock_status` go straight to `super` and behave as before.
- The dashboard gets a "Stock status" filter plus Available and Low stock threshold columns.
- The PR also adds StrykerJS mutation testing setup and reports.

It checks out as sound:
- The SQL is built only from constants.
- The `HAVING` and ordering are correct.
- Soft-deleted levels are excluded.
- The available-quantity rule matches the dashboard's `getStockStatus`.
- The validator keeps `stock_status` out of `$and` / `$or`, as the PR says.
- The translation keys all exist.

## Findings

**Medium**
1. **Large ids list can fail outright.** In `inventory-module.ts` (`listAndCountInventoryItems`), `{ id: sortedIds }` becomes one `IN (...)` list. Postgres allows 65,535 bind parameters, so a catalog with more matching items than that fails with an error instead of just getting slower. The `shortcut:` comment says "tens of thousands" and suggests it only slows down. Either chunk the list or do the other-filter intersection in the SQL query, and fix the comment.

**Low**
2. **Prototype keys pass the status check.** In `listIdsByStockStatus_`, `!(status in conditions)` accepts `"toString"` and `"constructor"`, because `in` also checks the prototype chain. A function's source then ends up in the SQL string. The API's zod enum blocks this, so only direct module callers can reach it. Use `Object.hasOwn(conditions, status)`.
3. **`withDeleted` is ignored.** The SQL hard-codes `deleted_at IS NULL`, so `config.withDeleted` does nothing when `stock_status` is set. Worth a doc note or a guard.
4. **Hard-coded line range.** `stryker.config.json` mutates `inventory-module.ts:443-553`, which goes stale on the next edit. Mutation testing will quietly cover the wrong code.
5. **`stryker-build.cjs` edits tracked source.** It rewrites `inventory-module.ts` in place and leaves the tree dirty after an aborted run. It is idempotent, but it's easy to commit by accident.

**Nits**
- **Dashboard URL param:** `stock_status` from the URL is cast with `as` and not validated. A hand-edited bad value returns a 400 from the API.
- **Root dev dependencies:** Stryker is a root dependency and adds about 1,250 lines to `yarn.lock`. Putting it under `packages/modules/inventory` would keep that out of everyone else's install.
- **Location filter:** it is documented that status always covers all locations. A reviewer might still expect location-scoped status when that filter is on.

Approve after the large-list fix (#1) and the one-line `Object.hasOwn` change (#2). The rest can be follow-ups.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5-5 2026-11-17 16:18:58Z)**_

Yes, it's fixable, and the fix is small. I'd go with a variant of option 1 below.

## Why it fails
`listAndCountInventoryItems` passes `{ id: sortedIds }` into `inventoryItemService_.list(...)`. That becomes `WHERE id IN ($1, $2, ... $N)`, so it breaks once N passes about 65k, the Postgres bind-parameter limit.

## Fix options

**1. Skip the intersection when there are no other filters (easiest).**
The common case is only `stock_status` plus paging. There, `sortedIds` is already the final ordered list, so the second query adds nothing. Only run the intersection when `otherFilters` actually has keys.

```ts
const hasOtherFilters = Object.keys(otherFilters).length > 0

let ids = sortedIds
if (hasOtherFilters) {
  const matching = await this.inventoryItemService_.list(
    { $and: [otherFilters, { id: sortedIds }] },
    { select: ["id"] },
    context
  )
  const matchingIds = new Set(matching.map((item) => item.id))
  ids = sortedIds.filter((id) => matchingIds.has(id))
}
```

The page load at the end is safe because `pageIds` is at most `take`, which is 20 in the dashboard.

**2. Chunk the intersection.**
When other filters are present, run the `id IN` check in batches of about 10,000 and merge the results.

```ts
const matchingIds = new Set<string>()
for (let i = 0; i < sortedIds.length; i += 10_000) {
  const chunk = await this.inventoryItemService_.list(
    { $and: [otherFilters, { id: sortedIds.slice(i, i + 10_000) }] },
    { select: ["id"] },
    context
  )
  chunk.forEach((item) => matchingIds.add(item.id))
}
```

Doing both fully removes the limit. It costs one extra query per 10k matching items, and only when a filter like `q` is combined with `stock_status`.

## What I'd suggest
Do both, since it's about 10 lines. Then add a test that the module and HTTP specs don't cover yet: more than 10,000 low-stock items with a filter set. The existing tests probably only use a handful of items. Also update the `shortcut:` comment to say the cost is time, not failure.
